Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The yotsugana are two distinct syllables, as they are in Tokyo, but Kansai speakers tend to pronounce じ /zi/ and ず /zu/ as [ʑi] and [zu] in place of _____ [dʑi] and [dzɯ]
Kansai dialect.fact: The yotsugana are two distinct syllables, as they are in Tokyo, but Kansai speakers tend to pronounce じ /zi/ and ず /zu/ as [ʑi] and [zu] in place of Standard [dʑi] and [dzɯ].

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In provocative speech, /r/ becomes [r], similar to the _____ dialect
Kansai dialect.fact: In provocative speech, /r/ becomes [r], similar to the Tokyo Shitamachi dialect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The /r/ + vowel in the verb conjugations is sometimes changed to /N/, similar to colloquial _____ speech
Kansai dialect.fact: The /r/ + vowel in the verb conjugations is sometimes changed to /N/, similar to colloquial Tokyo speech.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The Kansai pitch accent is called the Kyoto-Osaka type accent (京阪式アクセント, _____-shiki akusento) in technical terms
Kansai dialect.fact: The Kansai pitch accent is called the Kyoto-Osaka type accent (京阪式アクセント, Keihan-shiki akusento) in technical terms.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It is used in most of Kansai, _____ and parts of western Chūbu region
Kansai dialect.fact: It is used in most of Kansai, Shikoku and parts of western Chūbu region.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In the _____ accent, the pitch between first and second morae usually changes, but in the Kansai accent, it does not always
Kansai dialect.fact: The Tokyo accent distinguishes words only by the position of an optional pitch drop, whereas the Kansai accent distinguishes words also by initial tones, so Kansai dialect has more pitch patterns than standard Japanese. In the Tokyo accent, the pitch between first and second morae usually changes, but in the Kansai accent, it does not always.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: High-initial accent (高起式, kōki-shiki) or Flat-straight accent (平進式, _____-shiki) The high pitch appears on the first mora and the others are low: H-L, H-L-L, H-L-L-L, etc
Kansai dialect.fact: High-initial accent (高起式, kōki-shiki) or Flat-straight accent (平進式, Heishin-shiki) The high pitch appears on the first mora and the others are low: H-L, H-L-L, H-L-L-L, etc.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Low-initial accent (低起式, teiki-shiki) or _____ accent (上昇式, Jōshō-shiki) The pitch rises drastically on the middle set mora and falls again: L-H-L, L-H-L-L, L-L-H-L, etc
Kansai dialect.fact: Low-initial accent (低起式, teiki-shiki) or Ascent accent (上昇式, Jōshō-shiki) The pitch rises drastically on the middle set mora and falls again: L-H-L, L-H-L-L, L-L-H-L, etc.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: If high-initial accent words or particles attach to the end of the word, all morae are low: L-L-L(-H), L-L-L-L(-H), L-L-L-L-L(-H) _____ two-mora words, there are two accent patterns
Kansai dialect.fact: If high-initial accent words or particles attach to the end of the word, all morae are low: L-L-L(-H), L-L-L-L(-H), L-L-L-L-L(-H) With two-mora words, there are two accent patterns.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: This particular verb is emblematic of a native Kansai speaker, as most will unconsciously say 言うて /juːte/ instead of 言って /iQte/ or /juQte/ even if well-practiced at speaking in standard _____
Kansai dialect.fact: The geminated consonants found in godan verbs of standard Japanese verbal inflections are usually replaced with long vowels (often shortened in 3 morae verbs) in Kansai dialect (See also Onbin, u-onbin). Thus, for the verb 言う /iu, juː/ ("to say"), the past tense in standard Japanese 言った /iQta/ ("said") becomes 言うた /juːta/ in Kansai dialect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: For making their negative forms, it is only to replace -ない /-nai/ with -ん /-N/ or -へん /-heN/ (_____)
Kansai dialect.fact: For making their negative forms, it is only to replace -ない /-nai/ with -ん /-N/ or -へん /-heN/ (See Negative).

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: However, mainly in _____, potential negative form of ��段 godan verbs /-enai/ is often replaced with /-areheN/ such as 行かれへん /ikareheN/ instead of 行けない /ikenai/ and 行けへん /ikeheN/ "can't go"
Kansai dialect.fact: However, mainly in Osaka, potential negative form of ��段 godan verbs /-enai/ is often replaced with /-areheN/ such as 行かれへん /ikareheN/ instead of 行けない /ikenai/ and 行けへん /ikeheN/ "can't go". This is because /-eheN/ overlaps with Osakan negative conjugation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: This is because /-eheN/ overlaps with _____ negative conjugation
Kansai dialect.fact: This is because /-eheN/ overlaps with Osakan negative conjugation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In western _____, oru is used not only in humble language but also in all other situations instead of iru
Kansai dialect.fact: In western Japanese including Kansai dialect, a combination of an adverb よう /joː/ and -ん /-N/ negative form is used as a negative form of the personal impossibility such as よう言わん /joː iwaN/ "I can't say anything (in disgust or diffidence)". In western Japanese, oru is used not only in humble language but also in all other situations instead of iru.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: People in these areas, especially _____ women, tend to consider おる /oru/ an outspoken or contempt word
Kansai dialect.fact: Kansai dialect belongs to western Japanese, but いる /iru/ and its variation, いてる /iteru/ (mainly Osaka), are used in Osaka, Kyoto, Shiga and so on. People in these areas, especially Kyoto women, tend to consider おる /oru/ an outspoken or contempt word.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In other areas such as _____ and Mie, いる /iru/ is hardly used and おる /oru/ does not have the negative usage
Kansai dialect.fact: In other areas such as Hyogo and Mie, いる /iru/ is hardly used and おる /oru/ does not have the negative usage.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In parts of _____, いる /iru/ is replaced with ある /aru/, which is used for inanimate objects in most other dialects
Kansai dialect.fact: In parts of Wakayama, いる /iru/ is replaced with ある /aru/, which is used for inanimate objects in most other dialects. In Hyogo, southern Nara and parts of Wakayama, -よる /-joru/ is used for progressive aspect (See Aspect).

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In Hyogo, southern Nara and parts of _____, -よる /-joru/ is used for progressive aspect (See Aspect)
Kansai dialect.fact: In parts of Wakayama, いる /iru/ is replaced with ある /aru/, which is used for inanimate objects in most other dialects. In Hyogo, southern Nara and parts of Wakayama, -よる /-joru/ is used for progressive aspect (See Aspect).

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In Osaka, _____, Shiga, northern Nara and parts of Mie, mainly in masculine speech, -よる /-joru/ shows annoying or contempt feelings for a third party, usually milder than -やがる /-jaɡaru/
Kansai dialect.fact: In Osaka, Kyoto, Shiga, northern Nara and parts of Mie, mainly in masculine speech, -よる /-joru/ shows annoying or contempt feelings for a third party, usually milder than -やがる /-jaɡaru/.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: -ん /-N/ is a transformation of the classical _____ negative form -ぬ /-nu/ and is also used for some idioms in standard Japanese
Kansai dialect.fact: -ん /-N/ is a transformation of the classical Japanese negative form -ぬ /-nu/ and is also used for some idioms in standard Japanese.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The godan verbs conjugation before -hen has two varieties: the more common conjugation is /-aheN/ like 行かへん /ikaheN/, but -ehen like 行けへん /ikeheN/ is also used in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: The godan verbs conjugation before -hen has two varieties: the more common conjugation is /-aheN/ like 行かへん /ikaheN/, but -ehen like 行けへん /ikeheN/ is also used in Osaka.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: When the vowel before -へん /-heN/ is /-i/, -へん /-heN/ often changes to -ひん /-hiN/, especially in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: When the vowel before -へん /-heN/ is /-i/, -へん /-heN/ often changes to -ひん /-hiN/, especially in Kyoto.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: One is the normal imperative form, inherited from _____
Kansai dialect.fact: One is the normal imperative form, inherited from Late Middle Japanese.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The -ろ /-ro/ form for ichidan verbs in standard _____ is much rarer and replaced by /-i/ or /-e/ in Kansai
Kansai dialect.fact: One is the normal imperative form, inherited from Late Middle Japanese. The -ろ /-ro/ form for ichidan verbs in standard Japanese is much rarer and replaced by /-i/ or /-e/ in Kansai.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Polite suffixes です/だす/どす /desu, dasu, dosu/ and ます /-masu/ are also added やろ /jaro/ for presumptive form instead of でしょう /desjoː/ in standard _____
Kansai dialect.fact: This use of the adjective's stem, often as an exclamation, is seen in classical literature and many dialects of modern Japanese, but is more often used in modern Kansai dialect. Polite suffixes です/だす/どす /desu, dasu, dosu/ and ます /-masu/ are also added やろ /jaro/ for presumptive form instead of でしょう /desjoː/ in standard Japanese.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Ya originated from ja (a variation of dearu) in late Edo period and is still commonly used in other parts of western Japan like _____, and is also used stereotypically by old men in fiction
Kansai dialect.fact: Ya originated from ja (a variation of dearu) in late Edo period and is still commonly used in other parts of western Japan like Hiroshima, and is also used stereotypically by old men in fiction.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Desu is replaced by dasu in _____ and dosu in Kyoto
Kansai dialect.fact: Desu is replaced by dasu in Osaka and dosu in Kyoto. In Osaka, dasu and omasu are sometimes shortened to da and oma.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: There is another unique polite form omasu and it is often replaced by osu in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: Desu is replaced by dasu in Osaka and dosu in Kyoto. There is another unique polite form omasu and it is often replaced by osu in Kyoto.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: When some sentence-final particles and a presumptive inflection yaro follow -su ending polite forms, su is often combined especially in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: In Osaka, dasu and omasu are sometimes shortened to da and oma. When some sentence-final particles and a presumptive inflection yaro follow -su ending polite forms, su is often combined especially in Osaka.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In standard _____, -te aru is only used with transitive verbs, but in Kansai -taru or -taaru is also used with intransitive verbs
Kansai dialect.fact: In standard Japanese, -te aru is only used with transitive verbs, but in Kansai -taru or -taaru is also used with intransitive verbs. Other Western Japanese as Chūgoku and Shikoku dialects has the discrimination of grammatical aspect, -yoru in progressive and -toru in perfect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Similarly, -te yaru, "to do for someone", can be contracted to -taru (or to -charu in Senshu and _____)
Kansai dialect.fact: Similarly, -te yaru, "to do for someone", can be contracted to -taru (or to -charu in Senshu and Wakayama). In parts of Wakayama, -yoru and -toru are replaced with -yaru and -taaru/chaaru.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In parts of _____, -yoru and -toru are replaced with -yaru and -taaru/chaaru
Kansai dialect.fact: Similarly, -te yaru, "to do for someone", can be contracted to -taru (or to -charu in Senshu and Wakayama). In parts of Wakayama, -yoru and -toru are replaced with -yaru and -taaru/chaaru.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Other Western Japanese as Chūgoku and _____ dialects has the discrimination of grammatical aspect, -yoru in progressive and -toru in perfect
Kansai dialect.fact: Other Western Japanese as Chūgoku and Shikoku dialects has the discrimination of grammatical aspect, -yoru in progressive and -toru in perfect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In Kansai, some dialects of southern Hyogo and _____ have these discrimination, too
Kansai dialect.fact: In Kansai, some dialects of southern Hyogo and Kii Peninsula have these discrimination, too.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: However, keigo is no longer considered a feature of the dialect since _____ now also has it
Kansai dialect.fact: Keigo in standard Japanese was originally borrowed from the medieval Kansai dialect. However, keigo is no longer considered a feature of the dialect since Standard Japanese now also has it.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Even today, keigo is used more often in Kansai than in the other dialects except for the standard _____, to which people switch in formal situations
Kansai dialect.fact: Keigo in standard Japanese was originally borrowed from the medieval Kansai dialect. However, keigo is no longer considered a feature of the dialect since Standard Japanese now also has it.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: -Te okun nahare (also -tokun nahare, -toku nahare) and -te okure yasu (also -tokure yasu, -tokuryasu) are used instead of -te kudasai in standard _____
Kansai dialect.fact: -Te okun nahare (also -tokun nahare, -toku nahare) and -te okure yasu (also -tokure yasu, -tokuryasu) are used instead of -te kudasai in standard Japanese.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: For example, _____-san to yū hito ("a man called Mr
Kansai dialect.fact: For example, Tanaka-san to yū hito ("a man called Mr. Tanaka") can change to Tanaka-san yū hito.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: And to yū is sometimes contracted to chū or tchū instead of te, tsū or ttsū in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: And to yū is sometimes contracted to chū or tchū instead of te, tsū or ttsū in Tokyo.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Besides naa and nee, noo is also used in some areas, but noo is usually considered too harsh a masculine particle in modern _____
Kansai dialect.fact: Besides naa and nee, noo is also used in some areas, but noo is usually considered too harsh a masculine particle in modern Keihanshin.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The most prominent to _____ speakers is the heavy use of wa by men
Kansai dialect.fact: The most prominent to Tokyo speakers is the heavy use of wa by men. It is noted that the feminine usage of wa in Tokyo is pronounced with a rising intonation and the Kansai usage of wa is pronounced with a falling intonation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It is noted that the feminine usage of wa in _____ is pronounced with a rising intonation and the Kansai usage of wa is pronounced with a falling intonation
Kansai dialect.fact: The most prominent to Tokyo speakers is the heavy use of wa by men. It is noted that the feminine usage of wa in Tokyo is pronounced with a rising intonation and the Kansai usage of wa is pronounced with a falling intonation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In standard _____, it is used exclusively by women and so is said to sound softer
Kansai dialect.fact: In standard Japanese, it is used exclusively by women and so is said to sound softer. In western Japanese including Kansai dialect, however, it is used equally by both men and women in many different levels of conversation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It comes from no ya (particle no + copula ya, also n ya) and much the same as the standard _____ no da (also n da)
Kansai dialect.fact: In western Japanese including Kansai dialect, however, it is used equally by both men and women in many different levels of conversation. It comes from no ya (particle no + copula ya, also n ya) and much the same as the standard Japanese no da (also n da).

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The common Kansai dialect is spoken in Keihanshin (the metropolitan areas of the cities of Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe) and its surroundings, a radius of about _____ (31 mi) around the Osaka-Kyoto-Kobe area
Kansai dialect.fact: The common Kansai dialect is spoken in Keihanshin (the metropolitan areas of the cities of Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe) and its surroundings, a radius of about 50 km (31 mi) around the Osaka-Kyoto-Kobe area (see regional differences).

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: However, Kansai is the second most populated urban region in Japan after Kantō, with a population of about _____, so Kansai dialect is still the most widely spoken, known and influential non-standard
Kansai dialect.fact: However, Kansai is the second most populated urban region in Japan after Kantō, with a population of about 20 million, so Kansai dialect is still the most widely spoken, known and influential non-standard Japanese dialect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: However, mainly in _____, potential negative form of 五段 godan verbs /-enai/ is often replaced with /-areheN/ such as 行かれへん /ikareheN/ instead of 行けない /ikenai/ and 行けへん /ikeheN/ "can't go"
Kansai dialect.fact: However, mainly in Osaka, potential negative form of 五段 godan verbs /-enai/ is often replaced with /-areheN/ such as 行かれへん /ikareheN/ instead of 行けない /ikenai/ and 行けへん /ikeheN/ "can't go". This is because /-eheN/ overlaps with Osakan negative conjugation.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The emphatic particle ze, heard often from _____ men, is rarely heard in Kansai
Kansai dialect.fact: The emphatic particle ze, heard often from Tokyo men, is rarely heard in Kansai.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The emphasis or tag question particle jan ka in the casual speech of _____ changes to yan ka in Kansai
Kansai dialect.fact: The emphasis or tag question particle jan ka in the casual speech of Kanto changes to yan ka in Kansai. Yan ka has some variations, such as a masculine variation yan ke (in some areas, but yan ke is also used by women) and a shortened variation yan, just like jan in Kanto.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Yan ka has some variations, such as a masculine variation yan ke (in some areas, but yan ke is also used by women) and a shortened variation yan, just like jan in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: The emphasis or tag question particle jan ka in the casual speech of Kanto changes to yan ka in Kansai. Yan ka has some variations, such as a masculine variation yan ke (in some areas, but yan ke is also used by women) and a shortened variation yan, just like jan in Kanto.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The verb hokasu corresponds to standard _____ suteru "to throw away", and metcha corresponds to the standard Japanese slang chō "very"
Kansai dialect.fact: The verb hokasu corresponds to standard Japanese suteru "to throw away", and metcha corresponds to the standard Japanese slang chō "very". Some Japanese words gain entirely different meanings or are used in different ways when used in Kansai dialect.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Thus the phrase chō matte "wait a minute" by a Kansai person sounds strange to a _____ person
Kansai dialect.fact: Thus the phrase chō matte "wait a minute" by a Kansai person sounds strange to a Tokyo person.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Basically equivalent to the standard baka "idiot, fool", aho is both a term of reproach and a term of endearment to the Kansai speaker, somewhat like _____ twit or silly
Kansai dialect.fact: Basically equivalent to the standard baka "idiot, fool", aho is both a term of reproach and a term of endearment to the Kansai speaker, somewhat like English twit or silly.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Where a _____ citizen would almost certainly object to being called baka, being called aho by a Kansai person is not necessarily much of an insult
Kansai dialect.fact: Where a Tokyo citizen would almost certainly object to being called baka, being called aho by a Kansai person is not necessarily much of an insult. Being called baka by a Kansai speaker is however a much more severe criticism than it would be by a Tokyo speaker.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Being called baka by a Kansai speaker is however a much more severe criticism than it would be by a _____ speaker
Kansai dialect.fact: Where a Tokyo citizen would almost certainly object to being called baka, being called aho by a Kansai person is not necessarily much of an insult. Being called baka by a Kansai speaker is however a much more severe criticism than it would be by a Tokyo speaker.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Jibun (自分) is a _____ word meaning "oneself" and sometimes "I", but it has an additional usage in Kansai as a casual second-person pronoun
Kansai dialect.fact: Jibun (自分) is a Japanese word meaning "oneself" and sometimes "I", but it has an additional usage in Kansai as a casual second-person pronoun.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It is also the characteristic of Kansai usage of honorific suffixes that they can be used for some familiar inanimate objects as well, especially in _____
Kansai dialect.fact: It is also the characteristic of Kansai usage of honorific suffixes that they can be used for some familiar inanimate objects as well, especially in Kyoto.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In standard _____, the usage is usually considered childish, but in Kansai, o-imo-san, o-mame-san and ame-chan are often heard not only in children's speech but also in adults' speech
Kansai dialect.fact: In standard Japanese, the usage is usually considered childish, but in Kansai, o-imo-san, o-mame-san and ame-chan are often heard not only in children's speech but also in adults' speech.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: This is supposedly said as a greeting from one _____ to another, and the appropriate answer is another Osaka phrase, maa, bochi bochi denna "well, so-so, y'know"
Kansai dialect.fact: This is supposedly said as a greeting from one Osakan to another, and the appropriate answer is another Osaka phrase, maa, bochi bochi denna "well, so-so, y'know".

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The idea behind mōkarimakka is that _____ was historically the center of the merchant culture
Kansai dialect.fact: This is supposedly said as a greeting from one Osakan to another, and the appropriate answer is another Osaka phrase, maa, bochi bochi denna "well, so-so, y'know". The idea behind mōkarimakka is that Osaka was historically the center of the merchant culture.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The latter phrase is also specific to _____, in particular the term bochi bochi (L-L-H-L)
Kansai dialect.fact: This is supposedly said as a greeting from one Osakan to another, and the appropriate answer is another Osaka phrase, maa, bochi bochi denna "well, so-so, y'know". The idea behind mōkarimakka is that Osaka was historically the center of the merchant culture.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Also, bochi bochi (H-L-L-L) can be used in place of the standard _____ soro soro, for instance bochi bochi iko ka "it is about time to be going"
Kansai dialect.fact: Also, bochi bochi (H-L-L-L) can be used in place of the standard Japanese soro soro, for instance bochi bochi iko ka "it is about time to be going".

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: In the Edo period, _____-kotoba (船場言葉), a social dialect of the wealthy merchants in the central business district of Osaka, was considered the standard Osaka-ben
Kansai dialect.fact: In the Edo period, Senba-kotoba (船場言葉), a social dialect of the wealthy merchants in the central business district of Osaka, was considered the standard Osaka-ben. It was handed down in Meiji, Taishō and Shōwa periods with some changes, but after the Pacific War, Senba-kotoba became nearly an obsolete dialect due to the modernization of business practices.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It was characterized by the polite speech based on _____-ben and the subtle differences depending on the business type, class, post etc
Kansai dialect.fact: It was characterized by the polite speech based on Kyoto-ben and the subtle differences depending on the business type, class, post etc.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: It was handed down in Meiji, Taishō and Shōwa periods with some changes, but after the _____, Senba-kotoba became nearly an obsolete dialect due to the modernization of business practices
Kansai dialect.fact: It was handed down in Meiji, Taishō and Shōwa periods with some changes, but after the Pacific War, Senba-kotoba became nearly an obsolete dialect due to the modernization of business practices.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Senba-kotoba was famous for a polite copula gowasu or goasu instead of common _____ copula omasu and characteristic forms for shopkeeper family mentioned below
Kansai dialect.fact: Senba-kotoba was famous for a polite copula gowasu or goasu instead of common Osakan copula omasu and characteristic forms for shopkeeper family mentioned below.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Southern branches of Osaka-ben, such as Senshū-ben (泉州弁) and _____-ben (河内弁), are famous for their harsh locution, characterized by trilled "r", the question particle ke, and the second person ware
Kansai dialect.fact: Southern branches of Osaka-ben, such as Senshū-ben (泉州弁) and Kawachi-ben (河内弁), are famous for their harsh locution, characterized by trilled "r", the question particle ke, and the second person ware.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: The farther south in Osaka one goes, the cruder the language is considered to be, with the local Senshū-ben of _____ said to represent the peak of harshness
Kansai dialect.fact: The farther south in Osaka one goes, the cruder the language is considered to be, with the local Senshū-ben of Kishiwada said to represent the peak of harshness.

Kansai dialect.subject: Women & Society
Kansai dialect.question: Kyoto-ben is divided into the court dialect called Gosho kotoba (御所言葉) and the citizens dialect called _____ kotoba (町方言葉)
Kansai dialect.fact: Kyoto-ben is divided into the court dialect called Gosho kotoba (御所言葉) and the citizens dialect called Machikata kotoba (町方言葉).
